page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this server features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the multi-core processing capabilities of the ARMv9 architecture. The instance achieves top-tier performance in multi-core CPU stress tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation using Clang. Memory subsystem performance is also in the top tier, with read-only cached small block bandwidth reaching 21,316.19 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 402.56 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, with Redis handling 362.69 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and certain LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing for small models, fall into average or weaker tiers.

The c8gd.48xlarge offers high compute density and local storage capacity, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high parallel processing power alongside fast local storage. The absence of simultaneous multithreading ensures predictable performance per core. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput web serving, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM64-based server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.7 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 384.0 GB of memory and 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, software compilation, and database operations, including Redis SET performance. However, single-core performance and small-model LLM prompt processing are more moderate. The lack of simultaneous multithreading ensures dedicated, predictable core performance. This instance is highly suited for high-throughput database operations, multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, and static web serving workloads requiring high-speed local storage.
